title: Video Relay Service & Telecoms Equity (Home/Office/Travel)
desc: Why Deaf BSL users cannot dial any number the way hearing people can — the per-organisation VRS contract model, third-party refusal, and the home/office/travel access gap.

figures.label: Ofcom rejected a universal ("unrestricted") VRS mandate on cost grounds
figures.value: Estimated annual cost £41.6–£113.4 million; proposed a "restricted basis" VRS instead
figures.source: Ofcom, Review of Relay Services consultation, para 1.17–1.18

figures.label: Only text relay carries a statutory universal-service obligation — video relay has no equivalent
figures.value: Universal Service Condition 4 (BT) and General Condition 15 (all providers) cover text relay (Relay UK) only
figures.source: Ofcom General Conditions of Entitlement; Ofcom text relay guide

figures.label: Ofcom fined BT for late text-relay delivery, showing GC15 has real teeth for text — nothing equivalent covers video
figures.value: £800,000 fine, Case CW/01129, breach period Apr–Sep 2014
figures.source: Ofcom enforcement decision

figures.label: 999 BSL is mandated for emergency calls only — no obligation extends to general/non-emergency calls
figures.value: Confirmed directly in Ofcom’s own Emergency Video Relay statement
figures.source: Ofcom, Emergency Video Relay statement, 22 Jun 2021; live from 17 Jun 2022

figures.label: 999 BSL call volume — figures not yet reconciled
figures.value: ~18,000 calls (Jul 2024–Jun 2025 service year, annual report) vs ~24,000 calls ("in 2024", press reporting of the same underlying Ofcom study)
figures.source: Sorenson/SLI Annual Report, Jul 2025; Liam O’Dell reporting, 30 May 2025

figures.label: 999 BSL is entirely data/connectivity-dependent, unlike a standard 999 voice call
figures.value: Requires "a good internet connection to either WiFi or a 3G/4G/5G connection" — the technical precondition for the home/office/travel access gap
figures.source: 999 BSL FAQ

figures.label: Nuisance calls degrade emergency VRS capacity
figures.value: One caller made 150+ calls in a short window; 400+ nuisance calls in a single month (Mar 2024), tying up interpreters and delaying genuine emergencies
figures.source: Sorenson/SLI Annual Report; Liam O’Dell reporting

figures.label: DVLA VRS contract — the cleanest single procurement-grade proof of the per-organisation funding model
figures.value: £30,000 for 12 months (24 Apr 2024–23 Apr 2025), awarded to D A Languages Ltd, continuing the "Interpreters Live!" platform
figures.source: Contracts Finder notice, published 13 May 2024

figures.label: Motability’s VRS is scoped to Motability enquiries only — not general-purpose relay
figures.value: Application status, lease matters, and complaints only, via Sign Solutions’ InterpretersLive!
figures.source: Motability’s own site

figures.label: DWP VRS covers all its own service lines but is DWP-internal only, not a route to any UK number
figures.value: 12,536 total VRS calls in the 12 months to Nov 2020 (PIP 25%, Access to Work 22%, Universal Credit 16%, ESA 14%)
figures.source: Disability Rights UK; BDA; EHRC legal-agreement page

figures.label: No ring-fenced national VRS budget exists — BSL VRS is folded into a general interpreting-services framework
figures.value: Crown Commercial Service RM6302 (7 May 2025–6 May 2028, 31 suppliers, 5 lots) places VRS in Lot 4 "Visual Interpreting Services" alongside face-to-face interpreting; no VRS-specific spend published
figures.source: GCA/CCS agreement page

figures.label: SignHealth’s BSL Health Access proved a genuinely universal VRS model was operationally possible — then NHS funding was withdrawn
figures.value: Launched Mar 2020 with £800,000 of SignHealth’s own reserves; 25,000+ conversations handled (61% GP, 18% hospital); closed at midnight 31 Mar 2021 when NHS England funding ended
figures.source: SignHealth press release; Civil Society; The Limping Chicken

figures.label: Scotland runs a 24/7 national VRS — the clearest UK-internal proof a broader model is achievable
figures.value: Contact Scotland BSL, running since 2015, handling 3,000–4,000 calls/month; England has NHS 111 + 999 BSL only, Wales has 999 BSL only
figures.source: BSL Advisory Board, Locked Out

figures.label: The BSL Advisory Board’s central recommendation is a national 24/7 VRS for England and Wales — a government-published concession the current model is inadequate
figures.value: Not yet accepted or rejected by government as of this research pass
figures.source: GOV.UK, Locked Out, 27 Nov 2025

figures.label: BDA articulated this exact thesis 15 years ago — nothing fundamentally has changed
figures.value: Early Day Motion 1438 (9 Feb 2011, 104 signatures) called for "an open, competitive market for video relay services" giving telecoms access "equivalent to the way hearing people use the telephone every day"
figures.source: UK Parliament EDM tracker

figures.label: No confirmed UK case of a bank, DVLA, HMRC, or insurer refusing a VRS/interpreter-relayed call on identity-verification or fraud grounds
figures.value: The closest documented precedent is Irish (Kalinova v. Permanent TSB, ruled indirect disability discrimination, €8,500 awarded, 2022) and an EU-wide finding (Romania/Croatia) — neither is a UK case; do not generalise to "UK banks do this" without a UK-specific source
figures.source: Irish Times reporting the WRC decision, 5 Jul 2022; European Union of the Deaf EAA implementation report, ~Jun 2025

figures.label: No UK-specific evidence found of workplace IT/firewall policies blocking VRS apps at work
figures.value: Only a US product (Sorenson "at Work") confirms this is a recognised friction category elsewhere — genuine gap in the UK evidence base, not a confirmed non-problem
figures.source: Project research pass, cross-referencing UK and US VRS-industry sources

figures.label: No UK-specific evidence found of VRS or 999 BSL failing specifically due to travel or mobile roaming
figures.value: Only the underlying technical dependency (999 BSL requires WiFi or mobile data) is confirmed; no documented travel-specific failure incident was found
figures.source: Project research pass

figures.label: No published, comprehensive directory exists of which UK organisations currently offer VRS access at all
figures.value: SignVideo’s "SignDirectory" and a separate signing-banks list are both partial and unaudited — the absence of a registry is itself evidence there is no universal entitlement, only piecemeal opt-in contracts
figures.source: Project research pass, cross-referencing SignVideo and provider directories

figures.label: US comparator: VRS is funded as a universal, any-number relay service via a national fund, not per-organisation contracts
figures.value: FCC interstate TRS Fund net funding requirement: $1,479,568,862 for FY2025–26
figures.source: Rolka Loube (FCC TRS Fund administrator), order dated 7 Jul 2025
